title: Investigation of salt-bridge interactions underlying salt activation of halophilic methionine sulfoxide reductase A.
authors: Chen, Shuhong; Liu, Lianghui; Zhou, Hailang; Kuang, Xiaoxue; Li, Ye; Liu, Rong; Yang, Jiawei; Cheng, Xiaoling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过MD模拟、突变和活性实验研究嗜盐蛋白HhMsrA中盐桥对盐激活结构和功能的作用，属于蛋白质结构计算与实验结合的应用研究，方法创新性一般但问题和方法均命中。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Halophilic microorganisms inhabit hypersaline environments where sustained ionic stress challenges protein structure and function, making salt-responsive enzymes important for cellular fitness. Here, we investigated the salt-bridge interactions that support salt-dependent activation of a halophilic methionine sulfoxide reductase A from Halobacterium hubeiense (HhMsrA), a key enzyme involved in repairing oxidized methionine residues. METHODS: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, mutagenesis analyses, enzyme activity assays, and circular dichroism (CD) measurements were used to identify key salt-bridge-forming residues and evaluate their contributions to the salt-dependent structural and functional behavior of HhMsrA. RESULTS: MD simulations and mutagenesis analyses identified Arg106 and Lys76 as prominent salt-bridge nodes, and charge-conservative substitutions at these positions largely preserved the high-salt activity profile, whereas non-conservative substitutions (e.g., acidic, hydrophobic, aromatic, or proline replacements) generally reduced activity. Moreover, combined proline substitutions produced a pronounced cumulative effect, leaving the enzyme with only minimal activity even under high-salt conditions. MD analyses further associated these site-specific salt-bridge interactions with the maintenance of the salt-adapted structural state required for HhMsrA activity. CD measurements further showed a strong KCl-dependent helical response in HhMsrA that was attenuated to varying degrees across mutants targeting salt-bridge-forming residues. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that salt-dependent activity of HhMsrA is supported by a small set of salt-bridge nodes that contribute to maintaining a high-salt structural state compatible with HhMsrA catalytic function.
abstract_zh: 引言：嗜盐微生物栖息于高盐环境，其中持续的离子胁迫对蛋白质结构与功能构成挑战，因此盐响应性酶对细胞适应性至关重要。本研究探究了支持来自湖北盐杆菌（Halobacterium hubeiense）的嗜盐性甲硫氨酸亚砜还原酶A（HhMsrA）盐依赖性激活的盐桥相互作用，该酶是修复氧化甲硫氨酸残基的关键酶。方法：采用分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟、诱变分析、酶活性测定和圆二色性（circular dichroism, CD）测量，以鉴定关键盐桥形成残基，并评估它们对HhMsrA盐依赖性结构与功能行为的贡献。结果：MD模拟和诱变分析鉴定出Arg106和Lys76为关键盐桥节点，这些位点的电荷保守替换基本保留了高盐活性谱，而非保守替换（如酸性、疏水性、芳香族或脯氨酸替换）通常降低活性。此外，联合脯氨酸替换产生显著的累积效应，使酶在高盐条件下也仅保留极低活性。MD分析进一步将这些位点特异性盐桥相互作用与维持HhMsrA活性所需的盐适应性结构状态相关联。CD测量进一步显示，HhMsrA中强烈的KCl依赖性螺旋响应在靶向盐桥形成残基的突变体中不同程度地减弱。讨论：这些发现表明，HhMsrA的盐依赖性活性由一小部分盐桥节点支持，这些节点有助于维持与HhMsrA催化功能兼容的高盐结构状态。
